|  |  |  | 2.5.3 | Unfair Contract Terms | 1. Terms and conditions shall clearly set out the respective rights and obligations of all parties to transactions in simple language. The use of technical terminologies/languages shall be limited or avoided in contract documents, where they are used, FIs shall ensure that these terminologies are clearly explained to consumers.  Contract terms shall be considered unfair where there is a significant imbalance in one party’s rights and obligations to the detriment of the other. The following amongst others are considered to be unfair terms;  a) Limiting the liability of the financial institution in the event of total or partial non-performance of contractual obligations; b) Excluding the liability of the FI in the event of its negligence which is detrimental to the consumer; c) Clauses that bind a consumer while the corresponding obligation on the FI is conditional; d) Termination of agreements or alteration of clauses without reasonable notice to the consumer; e) Limiting the financial institutions’ liability with respect to actions or commitments undertaken by their agents; f) Giving the FI the possibility of transferring its rights and obligations under the contract, where this may reduce the rights of the consumers, without their consent; g) Excluding or limiting the right of the consumer to take legal action should infraction occur.  2. Contract terms that conflict with regulations are null and void ab initio.  3. Consumers or other stakeholders are encouraged to report contract terms that are in conflict with any regulation. | The bank shall: 1. Draft contract terms in simple, clear language, avoiding or clearly explaining technical terms. 2. Ensure that contract terms do not create a significant imbalance in the rights and obligations of the bank and the consumer. 3. Avoid including the following in contracts: a. Limit or exclude the bank’s liability in case of non-performance or negligence. b. Make customer obligations binding while the bank’s obligations are conditional. c. Alter or terminating contracts without reasonable notice. d. Exclude the consumer’s right to take legal action. e. Transfer bank rights that reduce consumer rights without consent. 4. Recognize that any contract term that conflicts with regulation is void. 5. |  |  |  | 2.6 | Protection of Consumer Assets and Privacy | Appropriate measures shall be established to guarantee protection of consumer assets and privacy. Consumer’s financial and personal information shall be protected by FIs at all times and shall not be released to a third party without the consent of the consumer, except as required by law.  The following information are considered to be confidential and shall be protected at all times; Contact details, account number and balance, statement of accounts and any other information known to the financial institution.  The Bank shall establish guidelines to safeguard consumer assets and privacy against unauthorized access. The primary areas to be covered are:  Fraud: the need for adequate controls to be put in place to prevent incidences of fraud.  Data Privacy: the need for adequate controls to be put in place to prevent unauthorized access to consumers’ confidential information. | The Bank shall:  1. Establish and maintain adequate controls to protect consumer assets and personal data against unauthorized access, loss, or misuse. 2. Ensure that consumers’ financial and personal information — including contact details, account numbers, balances, and statements — is treated as confidential at all times. 3. Prevent disclosure of consumer information to third parties, unless required by law or with the explicit consent of the consumer. 4. Implement fraud prevention measures to safeguard consumer assets from unauthorized or illegal activity. 5. Put in place robust data privacy policies and controls to ensure the protection of consumer information from breaches or misuse. | Fraud, data breaches, legal/regulatory penalties, reputational damage | High | High | IT Security, Compliance, Operations, Legal | Information Security Policy, Access Controls, Data Protection Guidelines, Consent Management | Medium | High | Regular penetration testing, Employee background checks, Privacy training | Ongoing | Compliance / IT Security / Legal |
|  |  |  | 2.6.1 | Fraud | 1. Financial institutions shall establish policies and controls to safeguard consumer assets against fraud. These policies and protocols may include the use of sophisticated software and transaction monitoring systems to monitor the internal processes/operations of financial institutions. Therefore, key policies shall include: a) Segregation of duties: the initiation and conclusion of transactions shall not rest with an individual. Necessary hierarchical controls, second level authentications amongst others, shall be put in place to prevent fraud; b) Access to information: appropriate access control systems shall be established by financial institutions. FIs shall restrict and monitor access to customer’s data base; c) Security (physical and electronic): consumer data and records must be securely stored at all times and accessed only by authorized personnel; d) Adequate data storage infrastructure: specification of technical requirements for data storage infrastructure; and e) Periodic audit: financial institutions shall ensure periodic audit of control systems to ascertain adequacy and effectiveness to guard against breaches.  2. Electronic payment instruments/systems shall be embedded with safety mechanisms; institutions shall ensure regular systems updates to guard against possible security lapses. The CBN shall specify minimum technology standards for payments platforms.  3. Financial institutions shall perform periodic internal risk assessment to identify and assess data security risks on their systems.  4. Financial institutions shall enforce disciplinary action against employees involved in fraud and report same to the regulator. Where required, the CBN shall blacklist such employee from further employment within the industry.  5. Financial institutions shall promptly refund customers for actual amounts lost due to fraud with interest at the CBN prescribed rate unless it can be proved that loss occurred as a result of customer’s negligence or through fraudulent behavior.  6. Financial institutions shall require customers to update their details within the timeline specified by the CBN. Customers are obliged to update their records as need arises in order to ensure data accuracy and ultimately enhance protection. Financial institutions shall create convenient avenues through which customers can make these updates.  7. Financial institutions shall continually create awareness on fraudulent practices and consumers’ responsibilities to guard against such. | The bank shall: 1. |  |  |  | 2.6.2 | Data Protection | 1. All personal information of customers (including those with closed accounts) shall be kept in confidence by FIs. |  |  |  | 2.7 | Complaints Handling and Redress | Adequate measures shall be established to address disputes that may arise from interactions and relationships between the FI and the consumer. The existence of effective complaints handling mechanisms that are affordable, fair, timely, transparent, accessible and independent would enhance overall consumer confidence in the financial system. The primary areas to be addressed are:  Complaints channels: avenues for lodging complaints shall be readily available and easily accessible to consumers. Consumers shall be made aware of the various channels.  Complaints management processes or procedures: The processes and procedures for complaints management shall be simple and efficient supporting the effective resolution of consumer complaints. Consumers shall be made aware of the various recourse mechanisms.  Complaints redress: provisions shall exist for the fair redress and compensation of consumers in the event of wrongful treatment.  Collaborations with other bodies: effective collaborations with other dispute resolution bodies in the industry shall be established to ensure a full coverage of consumer complaints handling. | The Bank shall:  1. Financial institutions and Alternate Dispute Resolution institutions shall provide consumers with information on available mechanisms for handling complaints. |  |  |  | 2.7.2 | Complaints Management Processes or Procedures | 1. Financial institutions shall have clear procedures (including timelines which must be in accordance with minimum standards set by CBN) for receiving and resolving complaints. FIs are expected to automate their complaints management processes or procedures.  2. Financial institutions shall establish and implement effective and transparent processes for handling complaints.  3. The complaints management processes of financial institutions shall include proactive measures to minimize the incidences of complaints. Complaints statistics shall be published in financial statements of FIs.  4. Consumer complaints shall first be lodged with the relevant FIs and only be escalated to alternate dispute resolution organs in the event that the consumer is dissatisfied or the complaint is not resolved within the stipulated time.  5. If complaints are not resolved by the financial institution or consumers are dissatisfied with the outcome of the complaints handling process, the FIs must inform consumers of the alternative recourse mechanisms available, and the process involved in seeking redress through these channels.  6. To avoid duplication of effort by ADRs, consumers shall lodge complaints with one ADR at a time and state categorically where complaints have earlier been reported to other ADRs as well as provide the decision reached.  7. Financial institutions shall provide consumers with status update on complaints. Consequently, the following must be addressed in the course of managing a consumer complaints: a) The timelines stipulated by the CBN; b) Financial institution’s acknowledgement of complaints received stating the timeline within which a response will be made available; c) Provision of reference numbers for all complaints received; d) In the event of delays, reason for delayed resolution including status in the event that complaint remains unresolved at the expiration of the agreed/ communicated resolution or response timeline; e) For complaints that have been resolved, resolution shall be provided in writing and acknowledged by the consumer. It is also advised that the consumer’s concurrence or objection is sought or obtained within a stipulated time.  8. To ensure easy resolution of complaints, the CBN may place a time limit or bar for lodging consumer complaints. However, time restrictions shall not apply in exceptional cases such as fraud.  9. ADRs shall not investigate cases concurrently with financial institutions; a case shall be admissible at the ADR only after a decision has been made by the FI. It is upon dissatisfaction with the decisions that such consumer may proceed to an alternate dispute resolution institution.  10. |  |  |  | 2.8.1 | Free market | 1. The CBN shall encourage product development by financial institutions to enable consumers have access to variety of innovative products and services.  2. | 5 |  | CBN Consumer Protection Regulations | 3 | FAIR TREATMENT OF CONSUMERS |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  | 3.1 | GENERAL PROVISIONS | Institutions shall comply with the following provisions to ensure fair treatment of consumers:  3.1.1 Treat consumers equitably without bias at all stages of the relationship. 3.1.2 Give consumers who meet the minimum legal and non – discriminatory eligibility requirements, equal access to basic services without regard to their social status, physical ability, marital status, gender, age, religion, tribe or ideology. 3.1.3 Consider the needs of the financially excluded, including the vulnerable groups such as low-income consumers, women, seniors, physically challenged and the non-literate in the development and implementation of their business models, strategies and processes. | The Bank shall:  1. Treat all consumers fairly and without discrimination at every stage of their interaction.  2. Provide equal access to basic services for all eligible consumers, regardless of status or identity.  3. Design and implement services that also consider the needs of vulnerable and financially excluded groups (e.g., low-income earners, women, elderly, physically challenged, and non-literate individuals). | Failure to uphold fairness and non-discrimination may result in reputational damage, customer complaints, regulatory penalties, and loss of consumer trust. | Medium | High | Chief Customer Experience Officer, Head of Retail/Consumer Banking, Compliance Officer, CSR/Financial Inclusion Officer | - Develop inclusive service policies and procedures. - Train staff on equitable treatment and non-discrimination. - Provide alternative access channels for vulnerable groups (e.g., USSD, local language support). - Monitor and report consumer complaints and resolution trends. | Low | Medium | - Conduct regular audits on customer interaction points.  - Include fairness and inclusion KPIs in staff performance appraisals.  - Launch financial literacy and inclusion programs.  - Establish feedback mechanisms accessible to all consumer categories. | Ongoing | Retail Banking Teams, Training Department, Customer Service, Compliance, ESG/CSR Desk |
|  |  |  | 3.2 | EQUITY | It shall be the duty of Institutions to treat consumers equitably always. Therefore, Institutions shall:  3.2.1 Treat consumers with courtesy and respect and shall not engage in practices such as threats, intimidation, use of abusive or offensive language, humiliation, misrepresentation, deception or unfair inducements. 3.2.2 Apply lending fees on disbursed amounts only in respect of term loans, except for fees which are normally applicable on undisbursed portions. 3.2.3 Apply non-credit related fees/charges on an account only to the extent of the balance in the account, and defer the outstanding fees/charges until the account is funded and the customer notified of the deferred fees/charges. 3.2.4 Promptly oblige consumers’ request for account closure or to switch providers, without unreasonable closing/switching barriers. 3.2.5 Ensure that variations to contracts including interest rate, fees or charges are only made if expressly provided for in the contract and shall notify consumer of any such variation. 3.2.6 Respond to customers’ enquiries/requests within five (5) working days of receiving the enquiries/requests. 3.2.7 Communicate a decision (acceptance or decline) on applications for waivers, extensions, and other concessions to a customer within ten (10) working days, otherwise the application shall be deemed to have been granted. 3.2.8 Not act in a manner that is inconsistent with the terms and conditions of their contracts with their customers. 3.2.9 Not seek repayment or withhold, in part or in full, customer’s funds to secure repayment before the due date, except with the written authorization of the customer. 3.2.10 Not charge early liquidation fees for consumer and SME loans with variable interest rate. | The Bank shall:  1. Treat all customers with respect and avoid threats, deception, or unfair practices.  2. Only charge lending fees on actual loan amounts disbursed (unless otherwise specified).  3. Only apply non-credit fees up to the available balance and defer the rest, with clear customer notification.  4. Allow customers to close accounts or switch providers easily, without delays or hurdles.  5. Notify customers of any contract changes only if stated in the contract and with proper notice.  6. Respond to all customer enquiries/requests within 5 working days.  7. Communicate decisions on waivers/concessions within 10 working days, or such requests are considered granted.  8. Honor all contract terms and avoid acting contrary to agreements with customers.  9. Do not withhold customer funds or demand early repayment unless authorized in writing.  10. Do not charge early liquidation fees on variable interest loans to consumers and SMEs. | Failure to comply may result in regulatory sanctions, customer complaints, reputational damage, financial penalties, and increased litigation risk. | High | High | - Head, Retail Banking - Customer Experience Manager - Legal & Compliance Officer - Product & Loan Operations - Collections Team | - Staff training on ethical customer interaction.  - Automated fee application rules.  - Account closure and switching procedures.  - Contract template review and approval process. - Complaint handling and escalation workflow.  - CRM system tracking timelines for all enquiries and waiver decisions. | Medium | Medium | - Daily/weekly compliance checklist on fee application and waiver response timelines.  - System alerts for pending enquiries or waiver requests.  - Internal audit on adherence to contract terms and switching procedures.  - Review and update fee application logic in core banking systems.  - Introduce dashboard for tracking compliance with notification timelines. | Immediate and ongoing | Compliance Department, Operations Control, Product Management, Customer Service |
|  |  |  | 4 | DISCLOSURE AND TRANSPARENCY |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  | 4.1 | GENERAL PROVISIONS | To promote transparency and enhance disclosure practices, Institutions shall comply with the following provisions:  4.1.1. Ensure that documents provided or made available to consumers shall: a. Be written in clear, legible and simple English language and in a minimum font size of 10. b. Be provided in a durable form for future reference. c. State the name, contact details of the Institution and the consumer. d. Contain a statement that the Institution is regulated by the Central Bank of Nigeria. e. Not be misleading or deceptive.  4.1.2. Put procedures in place to ensure that an oral explanation of the document is provided to the consumer in a language that he or she understands if: a. the consumer requests; or b. it is reasonably obvious that the consumer is illiterate or visually impaired or, for any other reason, cannot understand the document.  4.1.3. Conspicuously display in their banking halls and publish on their websites and internet banking platforms, accurate and up to date information on all their products and services. Such information shall include: a. prime and maximum lending rates; b. deposit rates; and c. exchange rates of foreign currencies.  4.1.4. Disclose to the consumer in writing, all Terms and Conditions of a transaction agreement. 4.1.5. Ensure that the disclaimer “Terms and Conditions Apply” or any other phrase conveying a similar meaning shall only be used if the terms and conditions have been explained and disclosed in the contract or in other medium accessible by the customer. The Institution shall at all times, draw the consumer’s attention to such disclosure. 4.1.6. Clearly explain technical terms used in documents to the consumer to aid understanding. 4.1.7. Agree with consumers on the communication channel(s) to be used for all correspondences and include the channel(s) in all contract documents. 4.1.8. Ensure that their websites and other information dissemination channels are functional and regularly updated with the current features of products and services offered. 4.1.9. Comply with the rates, fees, charges, or prices published or disclosed at the engagement points. 4.1.10. Inform consumers of applicable and indicative foreign exchange rates through customer engagement points and advise consumers to always check the rates before consummating foreign exchange transactions. 4.1.11. Bear all costs associated with disclosures to customers required by the Regulations, except for deposits and withdrawals by or on behalf of the customer. | The Bank shall: 1. Use clear, simple English (minimum font size 10) in customer-facing documents, and ensure documents are durable and personalized (with names, contacts, CBN disclosure, etc.). 2. Provide oral explanations for documents when requested or needed (e.g., for illiterate or visually impaired customers). 3. Clearly display on all platforms: up-to-date lending, deposit, and FX rates. 4. Disclose all transaction terms and conditions clearly in writing.5. Only use "Terms and Conditions Apply" if the T&Cs are explained and accessible.6. Explain all technical terms to consumers. 7. Agree on a communication channel with the customer and include it in the contract. 8. Ensure all dissemination platforms (website, mobile app, etc.) are functional and current. 9. Honour the rates and charges displayed at the point of engagement. 10. Inform customers of applicable FX rates at the point of transaction. 11. Bear the cost of disclosures required by law. | Non-compliance may result in poor customer experience, regulatory penalties, loss of trust, reputational damage, legal actions, and customer attrition. | High | High | - Head, Customer Experience - Legal & Compliance Department - Retail/Commercial Banking Heads - Corporate Communications - Product & Digital Banking Teams | - Disclosure templates approved by Legal and Compliance.  - Website and banking app update protocols.  - Periodic review of posted rates.  - Document accessibility processes.  - Standard operating procedure (SOP) for KYC and communication preference documentation.  - Internal audit checks on displayed and applied rates. | Medium | Medium | - Deploy plain-language checks during internal policy reviews.  - Conduct periodic mystery shopper audits for disclosure practices. - Embed compliance checklist in document issuance workflow.  - Update communication templates with multi-language support and accessibility considerations.  - Automate update logs and alerts for changes in rates/fees published online. | Immediate and continuous | Compliance Department, Digital Channels Unit, Branch Operations, Product Managers |
|  |  |  | 4.2 | ADVERTISEMENT | Institutions shall comply with the following disclosures for all advertisements and promotional materials:  4.2.1 The content of advertisements shall be factual and unambiguous, expressed in clear and simple language and shall not be offensive, misleading, deceptive, injurious, or exaggerate the benefits of the products or services being advertised. 4.2.2 The overall impression of advertisements shall not emphasize benefits of a product or service while de-emphasizing its associated risks. 4.2.3 Disclose their contact details in any advertisement or promotional material. 4.2.4 Clearly disclose details of the cost of a product or services, including all fees and other associated charges. 4.2.5 Fully disclose the nature and value of benefits, where an advertisement refers to, or is linked to other value adding benefits. 4.2.6 Not make references to unaudited financial statements. 4.2.7 Not mention names of competitors or make comparisons in their advertisements. 4.2.8 Unsolicited advertisements through emails, text messages, voice calls and other channels sent by or on behalf of a Institution shall be at no cost to the consumer and shall contain an opt-out provision for future advertisements. 4.2.9 Notify the Director, Consumer Protection Department of the CBN prior to the commencement of advertisement of product or service by submitting a description of the content of the advertisement. | The Bank shall: 1. Ensure advertisements are factual, clear, and not misleading. 2. Avoid exaggerating benefits or hiding product/service risks. 3. Display contact details in all adverts. 4. Disclose full cost of products/services, including fees and charges. 5. Clearly state the value and nature of any benefits tied to a product. 6. Not reference unaudited financials. 7. Avoid mentioning competitors or making comparisons. 8. Be free to recipients and must include an opt-out option from unsolicited ads via email/SMS/calls. 9. Notify CBN before launching any product/service advertisement with content details. | - Non-compliance may result in regulatory sanctions or fines. - Could lead to consumer mistrust and reputational damage. - Legal liabilities due to deceptive advertising or omitted cost disclosures. - May be accused of anti-competitive practices if competitors are referenced. - Failure to notify CBN could cause regulatory breaches. | High | High | - Marketing & Corporate Communications Department- Compliance Department- Legal Department- Product/Service Owners- Contact Centre Team | - Implement advertisement approval workflows involving Legal and Compliance. - Maintain advertising policy and checklist in line with regulatory expectations. - Establish review committee to vet content before publication. - Use standard templates to ensure inclusion of contact and cost details. - Opt-out system enabled and tested on all unsolicited communication channels. - Maintain a record of CBN notifications and approvals. | Low | Medium | - Quarterly audit of advertising content across all channels. - Conduct periodic training for marketing staff on regulatory requirements. - Deploy automated compliance checks for digital campaigns. - Maintain a compliance log of all advertisements and their approvals. | Immediate and ongoing with each advertisement or campaign | - Chief Compliance Officer- Head of Marketing- Head of Legal- Head of Products- Head of Contact Centre |
|  |  |  | 4.3 | PRE-CONTRACT DISCLOSURES | Institutions shall comply with the following requirements prior to the execution of any contract with consumers:  4.3.1 Disclose all terms and conditions of a product or service on offer, as well as the features, risks, benefits, fees and other associated charges. 4.3.2 Disclose in contracts, the possibility of variations in interest rates or foreign exchange due to changes in market conditions. 4.3.3 Disclose similar products and services within the Institution, to enable consumers make comparisons and informed choices. 4.3.4 Provide the consumer, a Key Facts Statement (KFS) in the format attached as Annexure A stating a summary of key information on consumer loans. 4.3.5 Allow consumers a minimum of two (2) days from date of receipt, to review draft contract before execution except where the customer waives this in writing. 4.3.6 Give a consumer a cooling-off period of three (3) working days after the signing of a credit contract within which the consumer may cancel the contract without having to pay any penalty or charges. However, the consumer may choose to waive the option by notifying the bank in writing. | The Bank shall: 1. Disclose all terms, conditions, features, risks, benefits, fees, and charges of the product or service before contract execution. 2. Clearly state in the contract if interest rates or FX rates may vary due to market conditions. 3. Provide information on similar products and services to help customers make comparisons. 4. Issue a Key Facts Statement (KFS) in the required format for consumer loans. 5. Give consumers at least 2 days to review draft contracts before signing, unless waived in writing. 6. Allow a 3-working-day cooling-off period post-signing for contract cancellation without penalties, unless waived by the consumer in writing. | - Regulatory non-compliance penalties. - Consumer complaints or litigation for lack of disclosure or coercion. - Reputational risk due to perceived lack of transparency. - Breach of consumer protection laws leading to enforcement actions. | High | High | - Legal Department- Product Managers- Compliance Department- Retail/Consumer Banking Unit- Credit/Risk Department | - Standardized product disclosure templates (including the KFS). - Mandatory pre-contract disclosure checklist. - Internal review of draft contracts by Legal and Compliance. - Staff training on disclosure obligations. - Automated systems to flag contracts not meeting the 2-day review or cooling-off rule. | Low | Low | - Quarterly audits of contract documentation and disclosure processes. - Consumer feedback channels to track violations. - System-enforced delays before contract execution to honor the 2-day review period. - Inclusion of a standard waiver template for customer use (if they choose to waive review/cooling-off periods). | Immediate and Ongoing | - Chief Compliance Officer- Head of Legal- Head of Retail/Consumer Banking- Head, Credit Risk |
|  |  |  | 4.4 | CONTRACTUAL DISCLOSURES | Institutions shall comply with the following requirements during the lifecycle of any contract with consumers:  4.4.1 Notify consumers of any transaction on their account immediately it is made. At a minimum, the notification shall include date, amount, payer, transaction reference, channel and the cleared account balance. 4.4.2 Ensure that descriptions in account statements are clear. At a minimum, it shall include, transaction reference, payer transaction channel, location and account balance. 4.4.3 Ensure that, at a minimum, credit contracts contain the following information: a. Key features and risks; b. Tenor of the contract; c. The nature, amount and method of calculation of any interest, fee or charge and when it is payable; d. The applicable Annual Percentage Rate (APR) to be calculated using the formula stated in Annexure B1 and B2; e. Notice of possible variations in interest rates, and how the consumer will be informed of changes; and f. Information on how to lodge a complaint to the Institution and escalate complaint to the CBN where necessary.  4.4.4 Provide consumer with monthly statements (or confirmation/investment advice as the case may be) for all products and account types, including loan accounts, special accounts and other related accounts at no cost. 4.4.5 Provide account balances to consumers on request. 4.4.6 Give prior notice of variation in interest rates to customers. At a minimum, the notice shall state: a. The reason for the variation; b. The commencement date; c. The revised repayment schedule (where necessary); and d. The alternatives available such as concession, restructuring, re-negotiation, opt-out or termination of the contract.  4.4.7 Ensure that variations in interest shall only be implemented after requisite notification to consumers: 10 working days (DMB) and 5 working days for other Institutions. | The Bank shall: 1. Send instant alerts to customers for every transaction, showing date, amount, payer, channel, reference, and new balance. 2. Make sure account statements are clear and include transaction reference, payer, channel, location, and balance. 3. Ensure credit contracts show key features, risks, tenor, interest/fees/charges (with calculations), APR (as per formula), rate variation process, and complaint channels. 4. Provide monthly statements (or confirmation/advice) for all account and product types (loans, investments, etc.) free of charge. 5. Provide account balances when requested by customers. 6. Before changing interest rates, give prior notice stating: reason, start date, revised schedule, and customer options (restructure, renegotiate, exit, etc.). 7. Delay interest changes until 10 working days’ notice for DMBs or 5 working days for others has been given. | Failure to comply can lead to customer complaints, regulatory sanctions, disputes over unfair charges or changes in terms, reputational damage, and class-action lawsuits. | High | High | - Legal and Compliance Unit - Retail/Commercial Lending Teams - Core Banking Product Managers - Customer Experience/Operations - IT/Alert Notification & Statement Delivery Team | - Automated transaction alert system.  - Template-based contract documents reviewed by Legal.  - System-generated monthly statements.  - SMS/email balance inquiry processes.  - Interest variation approval workflows with customer notification embedded. | Medium | Medium | - Regular review and audit of contract templates for compliance with APR disclosure formula.  - Automated enforcement of pre-notification for interest rate changes.  - Enforce statement clarity and quality checks.  - Customer feedback loop on statement clarity and transaction alert satisfaction.  - Track SLA for provision of account balance requests. | Ongoing | Compliance Team, IT Systems Admin, Retail Lending Head, Customer Communications Lead |
|  |  |  | 4.5 | For deposit products | a. minimum balance requirement and other limit on account balances or transactions where applicable; b. monthly maintenance fee, any applicable tenor for a term deposit and any penalty for terminating a term deposit early; c. savings withdrawal options; and d. any reason(s) and timeline within which the account could become inactive or dormant. | The Bank shall disclose the following clearly to customers when offering deposit products: a. The minimum balance required, and any limits on how much can be held or transacted. b. The monthly maintenance fees, the duration (tenor) of term deposits, and penalties for early termination. c. How and when customers can withdraw from savings accounts. d. The reasons and timeframes that would lead to an account becoming inactive or dormant. | If these requirements are not met, customers may feel misled, resulting in disputes, regulatory penalties from the CBN, customer churn, and reputational damage. | Medium | High | - Retail Banking Products Team - Compliance & Legal Department - Customer Service/Branch Ops - Marketing & Communications - IT (Digital Banking/Account Setup) | - Product disclosure templates and brochures.  - Account opening forms include fee and limit breakdowns.  - Dormancy notification process in place.  - Maintenance fee schedules published online and in branches. | Low | Medium | - Enforce standardised disclosure language for all deposit products.  - Include visual summaries (e.g. fee tables) in welcome packs.  - Ensure account opening platforms (physical and digital) include pop-up/mandatory acknowledgment of these key points.  - Trigger SMS/email reminders about dormancy before timelines elapse. | Ongoing | Compliance Lead, Retail Product Manager, Branch Ops Lead, Digital Banking Manager |
|  |  |  | 4.6 | DISCLOSURE ON DEFAULT OF CREDIT REPAYMENT | a. Institutions that are DMBs shall notify consumers within 3 days from the first day of default, through the agreed medium that a default charge would be applied on the account after 7 days from the date the obligation becomes due. c. Default charge shall be disclosed in customers’ statements of account separately from the interest charge. | The Bank shall: a. Notify consumers within 3 days of the first default that default charges will apply after 7 days of overdue payment. c. Disclose default charges separately from interest in account statements. | - Regulatory breaches and potential CBN sanctions for non-compliance. - Customer distrust and disputes due to unclear or delayed notification. - Reputational risk from customer complaints or legal action regarding improper disclosure or penalty application. | High | High | - Credit Risk Management- Collections & Recovery Unit- Legal and Compliance Department- Customer Service/Experience Department- IT/Software Team (Loan Management System) | - Embed notification triggers in loan management system. - Automated alerts (SMS, email, in-app) to notify customers as required. - Standard operating procedures (SOPs) for collections to ensure timelines are met. - Ensure statement templates separate default charges from interest. | Low | Medium | - Periodic compliance checks on loan notification procedures. - Review of customer communications logs. - Internal audits of loan default handling. - Training staff on required timelines and disclosure language. | Immediate and Ongoing | - Chief Compliance Officer- Head of Credit Risk- Head, Collections & Recovery- Head of IT/Business Automation |
|  |  |  | 5 | RESPONSIBLE BUSINESS CONDUCT |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  | 5.1 | GENERAL PROVISIONS | To promote good business practices, Institutions shall comply with the following provisions:  5.1.1 Conduct their business in a responsible, professional and ethical manner. 5.1.2 Train their staff to promote competence, efficiency and professionalism in the discharge of their duties. 5.1.3 Provide clear information about products and services, features, terms and conditions and the applicable fees and charges. 5.1.4 Provide and inform consumers of the channels to make enquiries and complaints. 5.1.5 Notify customers of circumstances or situations that may affect the terms of their contracts or relationships. 5.1.6 Display all applicable fees for electronic payment services with the option to accept or decline before a transaction is consummated. This should include a notice that third-party charges may apply. 5.1.7 Not impose any product, service or channel on consumers. 5.1.8 Not charge fees for issuance and renewal of products or services which have not been requested by the customer. 5.1.9 Not compel consumers to buy a product or service as a condition for the purchase of another product or service unless where the products or services are directly dependent. | The Bank shall: 1. Conduct all business dealings professionally, ethically, and responsibly. 2. Train staff to uphold competence and professionalism. 3. Provide clear, accurate product/service information, including terms, conditions, and fees. 4. Inform customers about available complaint/enquiry channels. 5. Notify customers of any change that affects their contracts. 6. Display all e-payment fees and allow customer consent before transactions. 7. Not force products/services on consumers. 8. Not charge for unrequested products. 9. Not compel bundling of products unless they're interdependent. | - Risk of CBN sanctions and legal penalties for failure to comply. - Potential customer dissatisfaction, complaints, and churn. - Reputational damage due to unethical or misleading practices. - Risk of class-action lawsuits or regulator intervention from bundled/forced product offerings. | High | High | - Legal and Compliance Department- Product Management Team- Customer Experience/Service Department- Marketing and Sales Team- IT/Business Process Automation Team | - Develop a Consumer Protection Compliance Policy. - Ensure product/service literature is standardized and approved before publication. - Implement staff training and compliance onboarding. - Automate fee display and consent features in digital channels. - Maintain and publicize a complaints resolution framework. - Regular reviews of bundled offerings and customer opt-in records. | Medium | Medium | - Conduct mystery shopping and customer surveys to validate compliance. - Establish a compliance helpdesk for customer complaints on ethics. - Perform internal audits and periodic compliance self-assessments. - Quarterly compliance performance reviews with department heads. | Immediate and Ongoing | - Chief Compliance Officer- Head, Legal and Regulatory Affairs- Head, Customer Experience- Head, Products- Head, Digital Channels/IT |
|  |  |  | 5.2 | RESPONSIBLE LENDING | To ensure that the capability of consumers to repay credits are professionally assessed, Institutions shall comply with the following requirements:  5.2.1 Include in credit risk assessment procedures, the type and circumstances for which a credit will be suitable as well as clear lines of authority for approving the product. 5.2.2 Before granting credit to consumers, assess their capability to repay in a sustainable manner taking into consideration their financial circumstances. 5.2.3 Ascertain the credit history of consumers from the Credit Risk Management System, Credit Bureau and other sources of credit reference before advancing credits. 5.2.4 Have a policy to deal with consumers who are in financial difficulty. 5.2.5 Monitor loan performance and upon early detection of repayment difficulties engage the customer to discuss alternative repayment options. 5.2.6 Not compel consumers to buy products or services, such as insurance or valuation from a particular third-party provider as a pre-condition for the grant of a credit facility, but can provide the option to choose from at least three (3) providers or any number as may be prescribed by CBN from time to time. 5.2.7 Ensure that guarantors confirm in writing that they have read and understood their commitments, potential implications and the maximum amount they are guaranteeing, and have either: a. sought and obtained independent professional advice before executing the guarantee; or b. declared that they do not need independent advice. 5.2.8 Provide periodic update to Guarantors on the loan performance to enable them to assess the likelihood of being called upon to discharge their commitments. 5.2.9 Issue Letter of Discharge at no cost to customers within 5 business days after liquidation of their loans, and where the loan is guaranteed, the guarantor shall also be notified accordingly. 5.2.10 Notify customers where their loan requests are declined. The reason(s) for decline shall be provided upon request. | The Bank shall: 1. Include credit suitability criteria and approval authority in credit risk procedures. 2. Assess a consumer's ability to repay before granting credit, considering their financial situation. 3. Check consumer credit history from CRMS, credit bureaus, or other sources before loan approval. 4. Maintain policies for dealing with consumers in financial difficulty. 5. Monitor loans and engage struggling customers early to find repayment solutions. 6. Not force customers to use specific service providers (e.g., insurance); offer at least 3 options. 7. Ensure guarantors provide written confirmation of understanding and advice status. 8. Send guarantors periodic updates on loan performance. 9. Issue free Loan Discharge Letters within 5 business days post-loan repayment and notify guarantors. 10. Inform customers of declined loan applications and provide reasons upon request. | - Regulatory sanctions for non-compliance with responsible lending principles. - Increased loan defaults due to poor credit assessment. - Reputational damage and customer complaints due to unfair practices or lack of transparency. - Legal liability from guarantors or consumers who were not properly informed. - Potential CBN penalties for compelling use of third-party services. | High | High | - Credit Risk Management Unit- Loan Approval Officers- Legal and Compliance Department- Customer Service/Experience- Loan Monitoring/Collections Team | - Incorporate responsible lending checks into credit policy and procedures. - Embed income and affordability checks in loan application systems. - Set automated CRMS and credit bureau validation before approval. - Develop SOPs for handling financial difficulty cases. - Train staff on third-party product disclosure rules. - Require written declarations and advice confirmations from guarantors. - Automate alerts for periodic loan performance updates to guarantors. - Automate discharge letter issuance within 5 business days. | Low | Medium | - Quarterly audits of loan files to check compliance with responsible lending requirements. - Review of system logs for CRMS/bureau checks. - Periodic staff training on loan suitability, disclosures, and guarantor rights. - Internal compliance reviews of customer notification practices (declined loans, discharge letters, etc.). | Immediate and Ongoing | - Chief Compliance Officer- Head of Credit Risk- Head, Collections & Monitoring- Head of Legal- Head of Customer Experience |
|  |  |  | 5.3 | SALES PROMOTION | To ensure that advertisements and promotional materials on products and services are clear and not misleading, Institutions shall:  5.3.1 Provide information that would aid consumers’ decisions. 5.3.2 Carry out marketing of products and services in an ethical and professional manner. 5.3.3 Ensure that sales and marketing staff are properly trained and competent to perform their functions. The staff should be knowledgeable in key features, risks and critical terms of product offering. 5.3.4 Establish a process to periodically check and monitor the competence and conduct of sales and marketing staff. 5.3.5 The remuneration of marketing/sales staff shall not be solely based on sales volume/target but must give consideration to the interests and circumstances of the customers. 5.3.6 Provide consumers with the option to opt out from receiving marketing materials. | The Bank shall: 1. Ensure all product/service ads and promotions are clear and not misleading. 2. Disclose adequate information to help customers make informed decisions. 3. Conduct marketing activities in a professional and ethical manner. 4. Ensure marketing/sales staff are well-trained and competent on key product features, risks, and terms. 5. Establish a system to regularly assess staff conduct and competence. 6. Sales staff remuneration must not be solely based on targets – it must reflect customer welfare. 7. Allow customers to opt-out of marketing messages. | - Regulatory sanctions for misleading advertising or unethical marketing practices. - Reputational damage and loss of customer trust. - Legal claims from mis-sold products or deceptive marketing. - Customer churn due to aggressive or unethical sales tactics. - Poorly trained staff may lead to non-compliance and increased complaints. | High | High | - Head of Marketing- Head of Compliance- Head of Human Resources- Sales and Product Teams- Customer Experience/Service Team | - Implement a compliance review process for all advertisements and promotions. - Develop and deliver regular training for all marketing and sales staff. - Enforce a code of ethics for marketing and sales. - Conduct regular performance assessments and competency reviews of staff. - Design a balanced scorecard for sales incentives that includes customer satisfaction. - Include opt-out options clearly in all promotional messages (SMS, emails, etc.). | Medium | Medium | - Periodic mystery shopper tests to verify ethical sales behavior. - Maintain an audit trail for customer opt-out requests. - Include pre-approval from Compliance before running any major sales promotion. - Establish feedback loops for customer reactions to marketing campaigns. - Include disclosure reviews in internal audit programs. | Ongoing (training quarterly, audits bi-annually, reviews prior to promotions) | - Chief Compliance Officer- Head of Sales/Marketing- Head of Internal Audit- Head of Learning & Development |
|  |  |  | 5.4 | DATA PROTECTION AND PRIVACY | To ensure data protection and privacy of consumers, Institutions shall:  5.4.1 Protect the privacy and confidentiality of consumer information and assets against unauthorized access, and be accountable for acts or omissions in respect thereof. 5.4.2 Obtain the written consent of consumers to collect and process their personal data for specific purpose and provide them with the option to withdraw the consent at any time. 5.4.3 Not transfer personal data of consumers to a third party without their express consent, except in compliance with a legal obligation. 5.4.4 Inform consumers whenever their data is exchanged with an authorized third party, stating details of the exchange. 5.4.5 Review data processing and privacy procedures to ensure that the purpose(s) for which initial consent was granted remained valid. 5.4.6 Keep accurate and updated data of consumers always. | The Bank shall: 5.4.1 Ensure customer information is secure, confidential, and protected from unauthorized access, and be accountable for any misuse or exposure. 5.4.2 Get written consent from customers before collecting or processing their personal data, and give them the option to withdraw it anytime. 5.4.3 Do not share personal data with third parties unless the customer explicitly agrees or there’s a legal requirement. 5.4.4 Always notify customers when their data is shared with any authorized third party, including who received it and why. 5.4.5 Regularly review data processing practices to ensure they still align with the customer’s original consent. 5.4.6 Keep customer records accurate and current at all times. | Data breaches, unauthorized disclosures, or failure to get proper consent can lead to heavy fines (NDPA/NDPR/CBN), loss of customer trust, reputational damage, and litigation. | High | High | - Data Protection Officer (DPO)- IT Security- Compliance & Legal- Customer Service- Operations- Digital Channels / CRM Team | - Data Protection & Privacy Policy (aligned with NDPA/NDPR). - Consent forms embedded in digital/onboarding journeys. - Encryption, firewalls, and access control protocols. - Periodic internal audits on data access logs. - Customer communication protocols and records. - Data quality and KYC validation processes. | Medium | Medium | - Implement automated data consent dashboards (opt-in/opt-out history).- Consent renewal prompts at intervals. - Data sharing logs with customer alerts.- Staff training on data privacy & compliance. - Real-time update validation for critical customer data (e.g., email, phone). - Periodic compliance reviews with NDPA/CBN standards. | Ongoing / Quarterly reviews | Data Protection Officer (DPO), Head of IT Security, Head of Compliance, Customer Experience Lead, Legal Department |
|  |  |  | 6 | COMPLAINTS HANDLING & REDRESS |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  | 6.1 | GENERAL PROVISIONS | The resolution of disputes shall be the responsibility of Institutions. Consumer complaints shall first be lodged with Institutions for timely resolution and redress. Institutions shall:  6.1.1 Develop documented processes on Complaints Handling that will guarantee fairness, transparency, responsiveness and independence of the complaint handling mechanism. 6.1.2 Allocate adequate resources for complaints handling/redress and the processes manned by skilled and well-trained members of staff. 6.1.3 At all customer engagement points, disclose channels and contact details for lodging complaints, timeframe for resolution, and options for escalation. Where it is not practicable to comply with this, refer customers to where the information required could be obtained. | The Bank shall: 1. They have a clear, written policy on how customer complaints will be handled. The policy must ensure fairness, openness, quick response times, and independence.   2. Adequate resources (budget, personnel, technology) are provided to handle complaints, and the team is made up of well-trained professionals.  3. At all customer service points (physical branches, digital platforms, ATMs, mobile apps), information must be made available on:– How to make a complaint– Contact details– Timeframe for resolution– How customers can escalate unresolved issuesIf not feasible in a location, direct the customer to where this information can be obtained. | Poor complaints handling could lead to regulatory sanctions, reputational damage, erosion of customer trust, and increased litigation or escalations to the CBN Consumer Protection Department. | Medium | High | - Customer Service / Customer Experience Team- Compliance Team- Branch Managers- Contact Center Managers- IT / Digital Channels Team | - Complaint Management Policy (documented and approved). - Dedicated complaints handling unit with escalation matrix. - CRM system for tracking and resolving complaints. - Complaint channels published on websites, mobile apps, branches. - Periodic staff training on dispute resolution protocols. | Low | Medium | - Publish complaint resolution SLAs (e.g., 5–10 business days) visibly across channels. - Auto-acknowledgement system when complaints are lodged. - Monthly review of complaint trends and escalations. - Regular training updates for complaint handling staff. - Internal audit review of complaint resolution performance. | Ongoing / Monthly monitoring | Head of Customer Experience, Compliance Officer, Contact Center Lead, Head of Digital Channels, Internal Control Unit |
|  |  |  | 6.2 | COMPLAINTS MANAGEMENT CHANNELS | Institutions shall provide multiple dedicated channels to receive and handle consumer complaints including verbal complaints. The channels may include letters, e-mails, telephone lines, social media and digital software platforms. The following requirements shall apply in the deployment of the channels:  6.2.1 Be effective, functional, efficient and accessible always. 6.2.2 Generate a unique identification number and acknowledge complaints within 24 hours of lodgment, including transcription of verbal complaints. 6.2.3 Accord special consideration to the needs of vulnerable groups, especially the physically challenged persons and seniors. 6.2.4 Provide emergency channels for reporting time-sensitive issues especially fraud-related complaints at all times. | The Bank shall provide multiple complaint channels, such as phone, email, social media, apps, and physical letters, including for verbal complaints.   1.  Ensure these channels are always working, fast, easy to use, and accessible.  2.  For every complaint:– Generate a unique ID number– Acknowledge receipt within 24 hours– Transcribe all verbal complaints.  3. Ensure vulnerable groups (e.g., physically challenged, seniors) are given special support when lodging complaints. 4.  Provide emergency channels (hotlines or 24/7 platforms) for time-sensitive complaints, especially fraud-related cases. | Failure to deploy effective, accessible, and timely complaint channels may lead to regulatory breaches, delayed resolution of fraud, customer dissatisfaction, reputational damage, and penalties. | High | High | - Customer Service/Experience Department- IT Department (Digital Platforms)- Contact Center Operations- Social Media/Communications Team- Compliance Unit | - Multiple complaint channels (email, SMS, call centers, social media, branch desks). - CRM or ticketing system that logs and tracks complaints. - Acknowledgement templates for complaint response. - Fraud hotlines available 24/7. - Complaint SOP (Standard Operating Procedures). | Medium | Medium | - Enforce automatic ID and 24-hour acknowledgment for every complaint. - Track and test functionality of complaint channels weekly. - Develop escalation framework for emergency fraud-related complaints. - Train frontline staff on handling complaints from vulnerable persons. - Audit all complaint systems for uptime and accessibility. | Immediate and continuous monitoring | Head of Customer Experience, IT Support Manager, Head of Contact Center, Fraud Risk Manager, Head of Compliance |
|  |  |  | 6.3 | INTERNAL DISPUTE RESOLUTION | Institutions shall establish Internal Dispute Resolution (IDR) structures and processes for the effective management of consumer complaints. The IDR mechanism shall satisfy the following requirements:  6.3.1 Be under the oversight of the Executive Compliance Officer or an equivalent. 6.3.2 Upon receipt of a complaint, communicate to the consumer within 24 hours, an acknowledgment containing: a. a unique identification or tracking number, b. contact details of the complaints desk, c. expected resolution timeline, d. escalation options; b. the right of appeal available to the complainant for a second level review by the Institution; and c. the right of escalation to the CBN, or other Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) avenues where the complainant is not satisfied with decisions arrived at.  6.3.12 A complaint shall be considered as resolved where the complainant has indicated acceptance of the resolution in writing to the Institution within 30 days after the receipt of the SRC, otherwise the complaint shall be deemed resolved and closed in the records of the Institution. 6.3.13 Where a complainant is dissatisfied with a decision communicated by a Institution, the complainant shall, within 30 days from the date of the receipt of the SRC, request in writing for a 2nd level review. 6.3.14 Upon receipt of a request for 2nd level review, the Institution shall review, resolve and communicate decision(s) within the Timelines for Complaints Resolution by Institutions as contained in Annexure D for second level review. 6.3.15 Identify recurring complaint types, identify their root cause(s), implement remedial measures, and generate a Root Cause Analysis Report (RCAR). 6.3.16 Prepare quarterly RCAR and submit to the Central Bank of Nigeria on or before 14th day of January, April, July and October respectively. 6.3.17 The RCAR shall contain the frequency of occurrence, identified root cause(s) and the remedial actions implemented. 6.3.18 Report complaints statistics in annual reports and the abridged Financial Statement in line with the approved format or any other format as may be prescribed by the CBN from time to time. 6.3.19 Institutions may outsource complaints handling functions subject to CBN approval. | The Bank shall:  1. |  |  |  | 20 | Gratification by and through agents | (1) Any person who corruptly—  (a) accepts, obtains or agrees to accept or obtain or attempts to obtain from any person for himself or for any other person, any gift or consideration as an inducement or reward for doing, forbearing to do, or for having done, or forborne to do, any act or thing, or  (b) gives or agrees to give or offers any gift or consideration to any agent as an inducement or reward for doing or forbearing to do, or for having done, or forborne to do, any act or thing in relation to his principal’s affairs or business, or  (c) knowingly gives to any agent, or being an agent knowingly uses with intent to deceive his principal, any receipt, account or other document in respect of which the principal is interested and which contains any statement which is false or erroneous or defective in any material particular, and which, to his knowledge, is intended to mislead his principal or any other person,  is guilty of an offence, and on conviction be liable to five (5) years imprisonment or a fine of not less than ₦200,000.00.  (2) For the purposes of this section:  “consideration” includes valuable consideration of any kind;  “agent” includes any person employed by or acting for another;  “principal” includes an employer. | The Bank shall ensure that no employee, officer, agent, or representative of the Bank shall—  (a) accept, obtain, agree to obtain, or attempt to obtain, for themselves or for any other person, any gift or consideration as an inducement or reward for performing, refraining from performing, or having performed or refrained from performing, any act or thing;  (b) give, agree to give, or offer any gift or consideration to any agent as an inducement or reward for performing, refraining from performing, or having performed or refrained from performing, any act or thing in relation to that agent’s principal’s affairs or business; or  (c) knowingly give to any agent—or, being an agent, knowingly use with intent to deceive the principal—any receipt, account, or other document concerning the principal’s interests that contains any false, erroneous, or materially defective statement intended to mislead the principal or any other person. |  |  |  | 98B | Official corruption: person inviting bribes, etc., on account of actions of public official | (1) Any person who‐   (a)   corruptly asks for, receives or obtains any property or benefit of any kind for himself or  any other person; or   (b)   corruptly agrees or attempts to receive or obtain any property or benefit of any kind for himself or any other person,  on account of‐   (i)    anything already done or omitted, or any favour or disfavour already shown to any person, by a public official (as defined in section 98D of this Code) in the discharge of his official duties or in relation to any matter connected with the functions, affairs or business of a government department, public body or other organisation or institution in which the public official is serving as such; or   (ii)    anything to be afterwards done or omitted, or any favour or disfavour to be afterwards shown to any person, by a public official in the discharge of his official duties or in relation to any such matter as aforesaid,  is guilty of the felony of official corruption and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.   (2) In any proceedings for an offence under this section it shall not be necessary to prove- (a) that any public official counselled the commission of the offence; or (b) that in the course of committing the offence the accused mentioned any particular public official; or (c) that (in a case to which subsection (1)(ii) is relevant) the accused believed that any public official would do, make or show the act, omission, favour or disfavour in question; or (d) that the accused intended to give the property or benefit in question, or any part thereof, to a public official. | The Bank shall ensure that no employee, officer, or representative of the Bank shall—  (a) corruptly ask for, receive, or obtain any property or benefit of any kind for themselves or for any other person; or (b) corruptly agree or attempt to receive or obtain any property or benefit of any kind for themselves or for any other person,  on account of—  (i) anything already done or omitted, or any favour or disfavour already shown to any person by a public official (as defined in Section 98D of this Code) in the discharge of official duties or in relation to any matter connected with the functions, affairs, or business of a government department, public body, or other organisation or institution in which the public official serves; or  (ii) anything to be afterwards done or omitted, or any favour or disfavour to be afterwards shown to any person by a public official in the discharge of official duties or in relation to such matters.  For the purpose of this provision, it is immaterial whether— i. any public official counselled the commission of the act; ii. any specific public official was mentioned; iii. the accused believed the public official would perform the act, omission, favour, or disfavour in question; or iv. the property or benefit in question, or any part thereof, was intended to be given to a public official.  Any breach of this provision constitutes official corruption and is liable to criminal prosecution and penalties, including imprisonment for up to seven years. | Employees or agents might solicit or accept bribes or benefits linked to official acts, exposing the Bank to severe legal penalties and reputational damage. | High | High | Compliance department | Anti-bribery policy; employee code of conduct; regular training on corruption laws; whistleblowing hotline. | Low | Medium | Gift and hospitality register; enhanced due diligence and monitoring of interactions with public officials. | Ongoing | Compliance & Legal teams |

|  |  | 8 | AML/CFT/CPF  Institutional Policy Framework | (1) A Financial Institution shall— (a) adopt policies stating its commitment to comply with Anti-Money Laundering (‘AML’), Combating Financing of Terrorism (‘CFT’) and Countering Proliferation Financing of Weapons of Mass Destructions (‘CPF’) obligations under subsisting laws, regulations and regulatory directives and to actively prevent any transaction that otherwise facilitates criminal activities, Money Laundering, Terrorism Financing and Proliferation Financing (ML, TF and PF); (b) formulate and implement internal controls and other procedures to deter criminals from using its facilities for ML, TF and PF; (c) adopt a risk-based approach in the identification, assessment and management of their ML, TF and PF risks in line with the requirements of these Regulations; (d) comply promptly with requests made pursuant to AML, CFT and CPF legislations and provide information to the Central Bank of Nigeria (“CBN”), Nigeria Financial Intelligence Unit (“NFIU”) and other competent authorities; (e) not in any way inhibit the implementation of the provisions of these Regulations and shall co-operate with the regulators and law enforcement agencies in the implementation of a robust AML, CFT and CPF regime in Nigeria; (f) render statutory reports to competent authorities as required by law and shall guard against any act that will cause a customer or client to avoid compliance with AML, CFT and CPF Legislations; (g) identify, review and record other areas of potential ML, TF or PF risks not covered by these Regulations and report same to the CBN; (h) reflect AML, CFT and CPF policies and procedures in their strategic policies; (i) conduct on-going due diligence and where appropriate, enhanced due diligence on all business relationships and shall obtain information on the purpose and intended nature of the business relationship of their potential customers; and (j) ensure that their employees, agents and others doing business with them, clearly understand the AML, CFT and CPF programme. | The Bank shall: (a) Create a clear policy showing their full commitment to follow anti-money laundering (AML), terrorism financing (CFT), and proliferation financing (CPF) laws. (e) Always cooperate with regulators and law enforcement and avoid doing anything that blocks AML/CFT/CPF work. (f) Send all reports required by law on time and do not help customers avoid AML/CFT/CPF checks. (g) Look out for new areas of risk and report them to the CBN if not already covered in the policy. (h) Make sure their AML/CFT/CPF policy is part of their overall business strategy. (i) Regularly check customer information and understand why the customer is opening or using an account. (j) Make sure that all staff, agents, and partners fully understand and follow the bank’s AML/CFT/CPF programme. | Inadequate oversight by the Board and senior management may result in weak AML/CFT/CPF governance, delayed policy implementation, poor regulatory reporting, and increased risk of non-compliance, enforcement actions, and reputational damage. | High | High | Board of Directors, Chief Compliance Officer (CCO), Heads of Business Units | - Develop and approve a clear AML/CFT/CPF policy - Train all employees on AML/CFT/CPF rules - Use risk-based KYC and transaction monitoring - Carry out internal AML risk assessments regularly - Monitor and update controls as needed | Medium | Medium | - Perform independent AML audits- Use automated systems to detect suspicious activities- Regularly update policies based on new threats- Present AML/CFT reports to the board | Ongoing, with mandatory annual review or when laws/regulations change | Board of Directors (oversight), Chief Compliance Officer (implementation), All Staff (execution) |

|  |  | 13 | Designation and duties of compliance officer | (1) Financial Institutions shall designate a Chief Compliance Officer with the relevant competence, authority and independence to implement the institution’s AML, CFT and CPF compliance programme. |  |  | 19 | Customer Due Diligence (‘CDD’) measures | (1) Financial Institutions shall undertake Customer Due Diligence (‘CDD’) measures when— (a) business relationships are established; (b) carrying out occasional transactions above the applicable and designated threshold of US$1,000 or its equivalent in other currencies or as may be determined by the CBN from time to time, including where the transaction is carried out in a single operation or several operations that appear to be linked; (c) carrying out occasional transactions that are wire transfers, including cross-border and domestic transfers between Financial Institutions and when credit or debit cards are used as a payment method to effect money transfer; (d) there is a suspicion of ML, TF and PF regardless of any exemptions or any other thresholds referred to in these Regulations; or (e) there are doubts on the veracity or adequacy of previously obtained customer identification data. (3) Financial Institutions are not required to repeatedly perform identification and verification exercise every time a customer conducts a transaction except there is a suspicion that the previously obtained information is not complete or has changed. | The Bank shall: (1) Perform CDD (i.e., verify customer identity and gather key info) when: (a) A business relationship is being opened. (e) There are doubts about the accuracy or completeness of earlier customer identity info. (2) CDD is not required when: (a) The transaction is clearly a normal use of a card (e.g. ATM withdrawal, card payment for goods). |  |  | 20 | Identification and verification of customers | (1) Financial Institutions shall identify customers, whether permanent or occasional, natural or legal persons, or legal arrangements, and verify the customers’ identities using reliable, independently sourced documents, data or information. |  |  | 24 | Failure to Complete CDD | (1) A Financial Institution that is unable to comply with the CDD measures pursuant to these Regulations shall—  (a) not be permitted to open the account, commence business relations or perform the transaction with the concerned persons; and (b) be required to render a Suspicious Transaction Report to the NFIU. |  |  | 27 | Reliance on intermediaries and third parties on CDD function | (1) A Financial Institution that relies upon another FI or DNFBP to conduct its CDD shall— (a) ensure that the Financial Institution and DNFBP are subject to and have measures in place for compliance with the record keeping requirements prescribed under these Regulations; and (b) satisfy itself that copies of identification data and other relevant documentation relating to the CDD requirements shall be made available from the third party upon request without delay. (2) A Financial Institution shall satisfy itself that a third party is a regulated and supervised institution and that it has measures in place to comply with requirements of CDD reliance on intermediaries and other third parties on CDD as contained in these Regulations. (3) Financial Institutions relying on intermediaries or other third parties who have no outsourcing, agency, business relationships, accounts or transactions with it or their clients shall perform some of the elements of the CDD process on the introduced business. (4) The criteria to be met in carrying out the elements of the CDD process by the financial institution referred to in sub-regulation (3) of this regulation are to— (a) immediately obtain from the third party the necessary information concerning certain elements of the CDD process; (b) take adequate steps to satisfy itself that copies of identification data and other relevant documentation relating to CDD requirements shall be made available from the third party upon request without delay; (c) satisfy themselves that the third party is regulated and supervised in accordance with core principles of AML, CFT and CPF and has measures in place to comply with the CDD requirements set out in these Regulations; and (d) ensure that adequate Know-Your-Customer (“KYC”) provisions are applied to the third party in order to obtain account information for competent authorities. (5) Notwithstanding the conditions specified in this regulation, the ultimate responsibility for customer identification and verification shall be with the Financial Institution relying on the third party. (6) When determining in which countries the third party that meets the conditions can be based, Financial Institutions shall have regard to information available on the level of country risk. (7) For Financial Institutions that rely on a third party that is part of the same financial group, relevant competent authorities may also consider that the requirements of the criteria above are met in the following circumstances— (a) the group applies CDD and record-keeping requirements, in line with programmes against ML, TF or PF; (b) the implementation of those CDD and record-keeping requirements and AML, CFT and CPF programmes is supervised at a group level by a competent authority; and (c) any higher country risk is adequately mitigated by the group’s AML, CFT and CPF policies. | If the Bank relies on another Financial Institution (FI) or Designated Non-Financial Business and Profession (DNFBP) to do CDD, it shall: (1) Confirm that the third party follows CBN record-keeping rules and can quickly provide CDD documents when asked. (2) Make sure the third party is regulated and supervised, and follows proper CDD procedures. (3) If the third party has no direct business/account relationship with the bank or its clients, the bank must still perform key CDD steps. (4) The bank must: • Get CDD data from the third party immediately; • Confirm CDD docs can be shared quickly when needed; • Ensure the third party has AML/CFT controls aligned with CBN rules; • Apply its own KYC checks on the third party to assist authorities if needed. (5) The bank remains fully responsible for CDD even if a third party helps. (6) When deciding which countries third parties can be based in, consider the country’s ML/TF risk level. (7) If the third party is from the same financial group, the reliance is allowed if: • The group applies uniform AML/CFT standards; • Group-level compliance is supervised; • Higher country risks are managed through group-wide policies. | Over-reliance on weak or unregulated third parties can expose the bank to poor customer verification, undetected ML/TF risks, regulatory breaches, and legal liabilities. | High | High | Relationship Managers, KYC Unit, Compliance Officer, Legal Department | - Only rely on third parties that are CBN-compliant and regulated - Conduct due diligence on third party’s AML/CFT framework - Sign formal agreements with third parties for CDD obligations - Require immediate access to all KYC and verification data - Maintain audit trail of third-party reliance justifications | Medium | Medium | - Use a third-party approval register for all CDD dependencies - Reassess third-party risk annually - Conduct random spot checks on CDD files from third parties - Limit reliance to third parties in low-risk jurisdictions or regulated groups | Immediately – before reliance beginsOngoing – with periodic reviews | Execution – KYC Unit, Legal, ComplianceOversight – Chief Compliance Officer, Internal Audit |
|  |  | 28 | Application of enhanced due diligence to higher risk customers and activities | Financial Institutions shall perform Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) for higher risk customers, business relationship or transactions including— (a) non-resident customers; (b) private banking customers; (c) legal persons or legal arrangements such as trusts that are personal assets-holding vehicles; (d) companies that have nominee-shareholders or shares in bearer form; (e) Politically Exposed Persons (‘PEPs’); (f) cross-border banking and business relationships, and (g) any other businesses, activities or professions as may be prescribed by regulatory, supervisory or competent authorities. | The Bank shall apply Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) measures to customers, relationships, or transactions that pose higher risk of money laundering or terrorism financing. These include: (a) Non-resident customers (b) Private banking clients (c) Legal entities or trusts used to hold personal assets (d) Companies with nominee shareholders or bearer shares (e) Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) (f) Cross-border business or banking relationships (g) Any other high-risk category directed by CBN or relevant authorities | High-risk customers or structures are often used to hide identities, move illicit funds, or avoid detection, exposing banks to legal and reputational damage. | High | High | Relationship Managers, KYC Unit, Compliance Officer, Risk Management Department | - Identify high-risk categories at onboarding using a CBN-aligned risk scoring model - Collect additional information (e.g., source of funds, wealth, business purpose) - Get senior management approval before establishing high-risk relationships - Perform more frequent reviews and transaction monitoring - Conduct site visits or verify customer declarations independently if necessary | Medium | Medium | - Automate flagging of high-risk customers in onboarding platforms - Integrate PEP screening tools - Conduct regular training for staff on red flags and EDD procedures - Maintain an updated internal EDD checklist based on evolving risk categories | Immediately – when onboarding any high-risk customerOngoing – periodic EDD reviews and monitoring | Execution – KYC Analysts, Relationship OfficersOversight – Compliance Officer, MLRO (Money Laundering Reporting Officer) |
|  |  | 29 (3-7) | Politically Exposed Person (PEP) | (3) Financial Institutions shall in addition to performing CDD measures, establish appropriate risk management systems to determine whether a potential customer or existing customer or the beneficial owner is a PEP. (5) Where a customer has been accepted or has an ongoing relationship with a Financial Institution and the customer or beneficial-owner is subsequently found to be or becomes a PEP, the Financial Institution shall obtain senior management approval to continue the business relationship. (5) If an existing customer is later identified as a PEP, get senior management approval to continue the relationship. (6) Find out and verify the source of funds and source of wealth of all PEPs. (7) Monitor PEP accounts more closely and report any suspicious activity immediately to the NFIU. | PEPs pose higher ML/TF risks due to their influence and possible involvement in corruption or misuse of public funds.
